_comment: Hook registration for the opencode coding agent (@opencode-ai/plugin, sst/opencode).
opencode has no hooks.json mechanism (Claude Code / Copilot) and no pi.on(event, ...)
subscription API (pi) either -- its Plugin type is a single async factory function
`(input, options?) => Promise<Hooks>` that returns ONE fixed object, keyed by hook
names (@opencode-ai/plugin's Hooks interface). So the bridge in
plugin/polyforge-hooks.js READS this file at plugin-load time and its two returned
hook functions loop over the matching entries below, converting each match into the
Claude Code-shaped JSON the hook scripts already parse on stdin. The hook scripts
themselves are UNCHANGED and shared with the other three runtimes (cc/codex/pi).
The matchers live here, in data, rather than inline in the bridge, for the same reason
pi-hooks.json/codex-hooks.json do: tests/pf-commit-guard.test.sh asserts that every
runtime's registration file routes pf_commit/pr/wrap/ship to pf-commit-guard and does
NOT route unrelated tools. A matcher hardcoded in JS would be invisible to that gate.
WHY THIS FILE LIVES INSIDE opencode/ AND NOT AT THE PLUGIN ROOT (a deliberate deviation
from pi-hooks.json / codex-hooks.json, both plugin-root siblings of pi//codex-plugin):
aihub#653's file_scope lock covers exactly plugins/polyforge/opencode -- NOT a new
plugin-root sibling file -- so everything opencode-specific this wi adds, including this
table, is nested under that directory instead of following the sibling convention.
'event' keys are opencode's own Hooks interface member names (@opencode-ai/plugin,
dist/index.d.ts). 'match' declares WHICH SUBJECT the matcher is applied to:
toolName -> input.tool   (tool.execute.before, tool.execute.after)
An entry whose 'match' disagrees with the event it is filed under is SKIPPED, not
silently tested against the wrong string -- mirroring pi-hooks.json's own rule.
TWO FACTS BELOW ARE EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED (aihub#653 measurement, opencode 1.18.30,
via the fast, non-chat `GET /experimental/tool/ids` endpoint on a live `opencode serve`):
- the built-in Bash tool's id is the bare string "bash" (no prefix, no casing quirk).
- the full built-in tool id set is: invalid, question, bash, read, glob, grep, edit,
write, task, webfetch, todowrite, websearch, skill, apply_patch -- none of these look
like an IR1 bypass door (a tool that takes an arbitrary OTHER tool's name/args as its
own argument, the way pi's `mcp`/`mcpScript` proxy tools do -- see pi-hooks.json's own
`deny` entry for why that matters). No analogous bypass tool was found, so no `deny`
entry is added here for one -- inventing a rule for a tool that was not observed to
exist would itself be a guess. Re-check this if opencode ever ships one.
A FOURTH FACT WAS INITIALLY UNCONFIRMED AFTER SIX LIVE-PROCESS ATTEMPTS ACROSS TWO
SESSIONS (chat round-trips and opencode-serve+curl against a real MCP server, all
inconclusive in this sandbox), THEN RESOLVED by reading opencode 1.18.30's own compiled
source (strings -a on the installed binary, not a doc and not a guess): the MCP tool
registry is built by `let X3=$.fn("MCP.tools")(function*(){...V[M0.toolName(E,K0.name)]=
{def:K0,client:k,...}...})` where E is the server key from opencode.json's `mcp` map and
K0.name is the tool's own MCP name; `M0.toolName` is exported as `()=>wB`, and
`wB=(Q,X)=>Z1(Q)+"_"+Z1(X)` with `Z1=(Q)=>Q.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g,"_")`. So the
exposed id is deterministically `sanitize(serverKey)+"_"+sanitize(toolName)`. Our server
entry is named "polyforge" (see mcp.json.template), so `pf_commit` is exposed as exactly
"polyforge_pf_commit" -- no other separator, no double-underscore, no truncation. The
matcher below is still written PERMISSIVELY (`(?:^|_)pf_(?:commit|pr|wrap|ship)$` rather
than a literal `^polyforge_pf_(...)$`) so this BRIDGE keeps invoking pf-commit-guard even
if a project renames the `mcp.polyforge` entry -- catching a case pf-commit-guard's own
prefix strip cannot (see below).
CORRECTION (aihub#653, caught by this file's own test, not assumed): pf-commit-guard's
prefix strip (hooks/pf-commit-guard, "base_tool = tool.rsplit(...)" onward) does NOT
strip an arbitrary server-key prefix. Precisely: line 585 is
`base_tool = tool.rsplit("__", 1)[-1]`, which strips ANY prefix ending in a literal
`__` (not only a literal `mcp__` one -- corrected again in aihub#653's code_review, this
file previously overstated it as "exactly three literal forms" for that first case),
then two further literal-prefix checks: `polyforge-pf_*` (Copilot) and `polyforge_pf_*`
(pi, and now opencode, since mcp.json.template's server key is literally "polyforge").
So the AS-SHIPPED path is fully gated end-to-end: opencode always emits
`polyforge_pf_commit` for our template, which pf-commit-guard's
`elif base_tool.startswith("polyforge_")` branch strips to `pf_commit` correctly. But if
an operator renames the `mcp.polyforge` entry to, say, `my_polyforge_server`, THIS bridge
still calls pf-commit-guard (matcher above still fires, since it has no `__` and does not
start with `polyforge-`/`polyforge_`) -- and, since aihub#659, pf-commit-guard's own strip
recognizes that case too: once "polyforge" was present anywhere in the ORIGINAL
(pre-strip) name and the two literal-prefix strips above didn't already leave a
recognized verb, the real tool name is recovered from its known trailing verb
(pf_commit/pr/wrap/ship) rather than assuming where the server-key portion ends. That
closed the renamed-server-key fail-OPEN gap this comment used to describe as open --
in two rounds: the first (code_change) covered prefix/infix/`__` renames but, because
the recovery ran as an `elif` mutually exclusive with the two literal-prefix strips,
still missed the shape where a rename KEEPS the literal `polyforge_`/`polyforge-`
prefix and appends a suffix (e.g. `polyforge_v2`, `polyforge_prod`); the second
(review_fix) closed that by making the recovery an unconditional post-pass gated on
presence captured before the strips run, so it is closed for all rename shapes now,
not just prefix/infix/`__` -- and out of aihub#653's file_scope; the fix and its pinned
tests (six differently-shaped renames plus a negative control) live in
hooks/pf-commit-guard and opencode-bridge.test.cjs. aihub#659 also wired this file's
opencode-bridge.test.cjs into CI and gave it a row in pf-commit-guard.test.sh's
cross-harness matcher table.
